raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-metrics`, the `TokenizerManager` records `sglang:startup_time_seconds` (per phase: `load_weight`, `kv_cache_allocation`, `scheduler_e2e`, `tokenizer_e2e`) and `sglang:startup_cuda_graph_time_seconds` (per capture phase) once the schedulers report their startup phases, and the engine logs the "Engine startup timings" line from the same values. Rust mode has no `TokenizerManager`, so a Rust-mode server exposed neither family on `/metrics` and never logged the timings. Everything else the frontend serves on `/metrics` comes from the scheduler processes' multiprocess files or from the frontend's own request metrics; the startup phases reach only the main process.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/engine.py`: in Rust mode, the main process records the startup-time metrics itself once `scheduler_init_result.wait_for_ready()` returns, through a new `_rust_server_startup_time_sink()`. The sink is a no-op without `--enable-metrics`; otherwise it builds the tokenizer collector class `resolve_collector_class(STAT_LOGGER_ROLE_TOKENIZER, ...)` picks, with `tokenizer_metric_labels()`, and returns its `emit_startup_time`. The default class is read from the `metrics_collector` module at call time, so a replacement installed after `engine` is imported (a stat logger, or a model package's own collector) still applies. The samples land in the main process's prometheus_client multiprocess file, which the Rust `/metrics` already merges.
- `Engine._set_startup_time` takes the sink callable instead of the tokenizer manager. The Python path passes `tokenizer_manager.set_startup_time` and behaves as before, including the timings log line, which Rust mode now logs too.
- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: `test_rust_mode_main_process_reports_startup_time` replaces `metrics_collector.TokenizerMetricsCollector` after import, as a model package does, and checks that the sink builds that class with the base labels and forwards to `emit_startup_time`, and that it builds nothing without `--enable-metrics`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no model forward or kernel code changes, and generation output is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: one collector construction and a handful of gauge sets at startup, on the main process only.

## Testing

- `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_rust_server_dp_ports.py`: 44 passed on this branch.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the two changed files passes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import run_scheduler_process

+from sglang.srt.observability import metrics_collector

+    STAT_LOGGER_ROLE_TOKENIZER,

+)
 from sglang.srt.observability.startup_time import build_engine_startup_time
 from sglang.srt.observability.trace import process_tracing_init, trace_set_thread_info

@@ -1098,7 +1104,7 @@ def _launch_detokenizer_subprocesses(

@@ -1109,7 +1115,7 @@ def _set_startup_time(
             ),
             tokenizer_e2e=time.perf_counter() - startup_tic,
         )
-        tokenizer_manager.set_startup_time(startup_time)
+        set_startup_time(startup_time)
         cuda_graph_timings = ", ".join(
             f"{phase}={duration:.2f}"
             for phase, duration in startup_time["cuda_graph"].items()
@@ -1307,6 +1313,9 @@ def sigterm_handler(signum, frame):
                 start_disagg_service_for_rust_server()
             )
             scheduler_init_result.wait_for_ready()
+            cls._set_startup_time(
+                _rust_server_startup_time_sink(), scheduler_init_result, startup_tic
+            )
             # Set up subprocess liveness watchdog to detect crashes
             processes = list(scheduler_procs or [])
             names = [f"scheduler_{i}" for i in range(len(processes))]
@@ -1349,7 +1358,9 @@ def sigterm_handler(signum, frame):
             # Wait for the model to finish loading
             scheduler_init_result.wait_for_ready()
 
-            cls._set_startup_time(tokenizer_manager, scheduler_init_result, startup_tic)
+            cls._set_startup_time(
+                tokenizer_manager.set_startup_time, scheduler_init_result, startup_tic
+            )
 
             # Get back some info from scheduler to tokenizer_manager
             tokenizer_manager.max_req_input_len = scheduler_init_result.scheduler_infos[
@@ -2077,6 +2088,20 @@ def _calculate_rank_ranges(node_rank: int) -> Tuple[range, range, int, int]:
     return pp_rank_range, tp_rank_range, pp_size_per_node, tp_size_per_node
 
 
+def _rust_server_startup_time_sink() -> Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], None]:
+    """Where the startup phases go when the Rust server replaces the
+    TokenizerManager: this process records the startup-time metrics the
+    TokenizerManager would."""
+    if not get_observability().enable_metrics:
+        return lambda startup_time: None
+    # Read at call time: a plugin or model package may replace the module's
+    # collector class with its own subclass after this module is imported.
+    collector_cls = resolve_collector_class(
+        STAT_LOGGER_ROLE_TOKENIZER, metrics_collector.TokenizerMetricsCollector
+    )
+    return collector_cls(labels=tokenizer_metric_labels()).emit_startup_time
+
+
 def node_hosts_rust_server() -> bool:
     """Whether this node contains a Rust listener rank, assuming Rust mode."""
     parallel = get_parallel()

@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@

 from sglang.srt.disaggregation.base.conn import BaseKVBootstrapServer
 from sglang.srt.disaggregation.common.conn import CommonKVBootstrapServer
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints import engine
 from sglang.srt.entrypoints.engine import node_hosts_rust_server
 from sglang.srt.environ import envs
 from sglang.srt.managers import disagg_service
@@ -214,6 +215,33 @@ def test_typed_config_carries_tokenizer_metrics(enable_metrics):
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enable_metrics", [False, True])
+def test_rust_mode_main_process_reports_startup_time(enable_metrics):
+    # A model package's override of the collector class, installed after
+    # the engine module was imported.
+    collector_cls = MagicMock()
+    with (
+        get_context().override_server_args(
+            enable_metrics=enable_metrics, served_model_name="m"
+        ),
+        patch.object(
+            engine.metrics_collector, "TokenizerMetricsCollector", collector_cls
+        ),
+    ):
+        sink = engine._rust_server_startup_time_sink()
+        sink({"load_weight": 1.0})
+
+    if not enable_metrics:
+        collector_cls.assert_not_called()
+        return
+    collector_cls.assert_called_once_with(
+        labels={"model_name": "m", "engine_type": "unified"}
+    )
+    collector_cls.return_value.emit_startup_time.assert_called_once_with(
+        {"load_weight": 1.0}
+    )
+
+
